analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md. Per the changed-range map, edits are the date bump, the Nemotron Super encoded-body cap wording (8 MiB to 40 MiB, `media_too_large`), and a JSON-response-format-with-tools sentence near line 530. The supplied units are head-side excerpts at lines 1214-2038, which contain none of the changed ranges. They are unchanged surrounding text about prefill geometry, deadlines, MTP, sampling, reasoning parsers, tool-call parsers, vision caps and MiMo. I cannot see the changed hunks directly, only the patch excerpt. No code, config, auth, attestation, encryption or coordinator contract changes are visible.

The claimed 40 MiB cap is described as holding one 25 MiB base64 part (about 33.4 MiB) and every body the transports deliver. If a real code change enforced it, it would loosen a request-size bound (an availability concern for T-010/T-029 style resource exhaustion). That code change is not in this batch. The doc says a charge the shared budget cannot hold returns a media-memory 503, so admission control reportedly remains. The JSON-with-tools statement is a behavior description with no visible security impact. The statements about the T-041 prefix-cache scope (coordinator-authored salt, no cache receipts for Nemotron Super local endpoint) are consistent with the canonical threat model.

Remaining question for integration: whether the code PR in other batches actually raises maximumEncodedBodyBytes to 40 MiB and still bounds memory via the media-memory reservation before decode. This needs checking where the code lives; it cannot be established from these doc-only units.
